# Twinthos

> Twinthos is a managed digital-employee company. Twinthos Brain is the persistent intelligence layer for a company's approved knowledge; Twinthos Workforce is the execution layer of cloud-based digital employees that work around the clock inside defined permissions. Promise: work handled, time returned.

## Definition

A digital employee is an AI agent that holds one written job, remembers the company it works for, works through the screens of the software the business already runs, keeps an audit trail of what it did, and escalates consequential decisions to a named human who is accountable for them. It is not a chatbot, not a per-seat assistant, and not a model. The model is swappable fuel.

## Notes (live, all updated 2026-10-21)

- [Did the cash machine really kill the bank teller?](https://twinthos.com/notes/atm-and-bank-tellers/) — Everyone says cash machines killed bank teller jobs. US figures show teller numbers rising for 25 years after the ATM arrived, and what that means now.
- [What an AI employee really costs per hour](https://twinthos.com/notes/cost-of-an-ai-employee/) — The tokens cost tens of dollars a month. The monthly fee is the visible part. The number that decides it is the time your team spends checking the work.
- [What a digital employee really costs over three years](https://twinthos.com/notes/digital-employee-cost/) — The monthly fee is the smallest number in the deal. Setup, the approver, the first failure and the exit sit outside it. Here is the whole three-year sum.
- [Chatbot or digital employee? What you are actually buying](https://twinthos.com/notes/digital-employee-vs-chatbot/) — A chatbot answers what you ask and forgets you. A digital employee does one job, remembers your rules and keeps a record. Here is the gap, and the money.
- [What is AI, and what can it actually do for you?](https://twinthos.com/notes/intro-to-ai/) — A plain-English guide for anyone who has never used AI. What it is, the three ways it changes an ordinary week, and what to hand over first.
- [14 questions to ask before you buy a managed AI agent](https://twinthos.com/notes/questions-to-ask-managed-ai-agent/) — A short list to take into the meeting. Every question has an answer you want and a reply that should worry you. Hear two worrying replies and you walk.
- [53% of small firms already let AI cover a full job](https://twinthos.com/notes/small-businesses-already-hired-ai/) — A survey of 729 owners found 53% let AI absorb a full-time role's workload, and nobody in the data was let go. The 65% who are tired kept the checking.
- [The US renamed AI to SI. Your work is exactly the same](https://twinthos.com/notes/super-intelligence-si/) — On 29 September 2026 US agencies were told to say super intelligence, not AI. What changed for a small business: the name, not the work or the questions.
- [What answering your phone with software really costs](https://twinthos.com/notes/the-2-dollar-ai-that-answers-the-phone/) — Google's Gemini 4 Argon is $2 per million input tokens. Here is what 600 answered enquiries cost in a month, and what still breaks when you switch it on.
- [Why the same customer gets two different answers](https://twinthos.com/notes/the-company-brain/) — Dell, SAP, Google, Meta and Workday all announced company memory in eight days. Your staff still spend 2.3 hours a week retyping what the business knows.
- [What an AI agent actually does, and how to spot a fake](https://twinthos.com/notes/what-an-ai-agent-actually-does/) — Four big firms shipped agents this autumn. Here is what makes one a real digital employee, and how to tell in ten minutes what you are being sold.
- [Why most AI projects fail before they start](https://twinthos.com/notes/why-ai-automations-fail/) — MIT found about 95% of generative AI pilots made no measurable difference to profit. The 5% that worked fixed the paperwork before they bought anything.
